items.title: Jim Galloway interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: I listened a lot to him. I saw him once live... you absorb influences and certainly he’s in there.

ctx.x: One thing they say is, “plays soprano sax in a lyrical style reminiscent of Sidney Bechet.”

Well I guess anybody who has ever decided to play soprano sax, if they’re at all aware of the origins of the music, they have to have heard Bechet. He was, after all, he was the first great saxophone soloist in jazz. Statement made. And I don’t think I particularly played like him, but you absorb influences and certainly he’s in there. I listened a lot to him. I saw him once live, when he toured in Britain obviously before I left, and I was transfixed by his playing. The hairs on the back of my neck actually…
Was he playing only soprano then or was he playing a clarinet at all?
